articles.title: Selling Indian Property to Another NRI? The Buyer Must Still Deduct TDS — at 12.5% or More
articles.excerpt: When an NRI sells property in India, the buyer must deduct tax at source under the non-resident rules no matter who the buyer is — there is no Rs 50 lakh threshold and no basic-exemption adjustment for the seller. A lower deduction certificate, obtained before the sale, is the main tool to stop excess tax being locked up until the return is filed.
articles.nri_angle: Two NRIs in the Gulf or the US routinely buy and sell family property in India between themselves; the TDS duty falls on the buyer even when both parties live abroad, and getting it wrong can stall registration and repatriation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
